newsitem.title: USA: Fed could take no action, but system RP possible.
newsitem.headline: Fed could take no action, but system RP possible.

text.p: With Federal funds trading at a soft 5-1/8 percent, the Federal Reserve could refrain from open market operations on Wednesday, but the central bank might add temporary reserves through system repurchase agreements to address next week's add need, analysts said.
"I think they can stay out of the open market because the funds rate is pretty soft," said Patricia Thrapp, vice president at Aubrey G. Lanston. "But there is a chance of an eight-day system."
Kevin Flanagan, first vice president and money market economist at Dean Witter Reynolds, concurred.

"It's sort of split down the middle between doing nothing and doing an eight-day system," he said. "They don't need to add reserves for the first half of the (reserve) maintenance period, but an add need remains for the second half."
Josh Stiles, senior bond strategist at I.D.E.A., said that while the Fed might want to roll over the overnight system it conducted on Tuesday, "it doesn't look like they need to.
"They got the permanent add tranche (by buying coupons) on Tuesday and funds are soft today; I think they'll stay out," Stiles said.
Analysts at MMS International, citing "no significant pressures in the system," said they, too, expect the Fed to take no action.
Fed funds were trading at 5-1/8 percent, below the Fed's 5-1/4 percent target for the rate, in early dealings.
-- (( E. Freilich, North American Treasury Desk 212-859-1679))
